value.body: A chartered accountant is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) who handles audit, taxation, accounting and advisory work. CAs work in audit and tax firms, in company finance teams, or in their own practice after taking ICAI's certificate of practice. Work includes statutory and tax audits, GST and income-tax filings, financial statements and advising clients.

items.label: Course stages
items.note: With 2 years of articleship under a practising CA (current scheme)

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Tally, Excel, GST portal, income-tax e-filing portal

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with ICAI for the Foundation after Class 12, or enter directly at Intermediate as a graduate who meets ICAI's marks criteria. Clear Intermediate, complete articleship and the required training, then pass the Final to become a member. Practising in one's own name needs ICAI's certificate of practice.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Direct and indirect tax (income tax, GST) compliance
Preparing financial statements under Ind AS
Reading and applying the Companies Act and tax law

value.title: At a glance
items: Many CAs spend a few years in a firm or in industry before starting their own practice.
The course is long and exam-heavy; more than one attempt per level is common.
Building a practice takes time; early income depends on the client base.
